chapters.title: One territory. Every critical function.
chapters.body: Dominion Energy powers 3.6 million customers across Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina, plus the Pentagon's feed and the world's largest data center market. Every function below emits machine data. This is the story of turning that data into agentic operations.

chapters.title: The demand shock in Data Center Alley
chapters.body: Over 53 GW of data center capacity is in contracting and nine of the ten all-time peak days happened this year. Grid reliability is now a hyperscaler SLA. Splunk ITSI and the Cisco Time Series Model can turn historian, EMS and AMI data into forecasts and early warnings.

chapters.title: Building the East Coast's largest offshore wind farm
chapters.body: CVOW delivered first power on March 23, 2026 and is 81% complete. Each quarter of delay costs about $144M. Turbines, offshore substations and vendor remote access become a new OT estate that has to be observed and defended from day one.

chapters.title: Carbon-free baseload for 80 years
chapters.body: North Anna is licensed to 2058 and 2060, and Dominion is preserving a path to an SMR with Amazon. Nuclear cyber programs need airtight evidence: portable media, critical digital asset baselines, one-way data transfers and insider risk.

chapters.title: A grid that is being "inhabited silently"
chapters.body: Dragos reports VOLTZITE (Volt Typhoon overlap) at Stage 2 of the ICS kill chain, and SYLVANITE inside a U.S. electric utility. OT ransomware is up 64%. E-ISAC logged more than 3,500 physical incidents. Watch the red pulses: these are the attack paths.

chapters.title: Splunk: the data fabric under everything
chapters.body: Dominion already runs Splunk Core, ES Premier and SOAR. Building on that, every SCADA historian, firewall, badge reader, turbine and IVR session lands in one Cisco Data Fabric powered by Splunk. Data that should stay where it is gets federated in place from S3, Snowflake and Azure. Edge Processor filters it at the substation.

chapters.title: Cisco Cloud Control: agentic ops with humans in charge
chapters.body: Cloud Control gives people and agents one login, one data layer and one system of action. Agent Builder connects ServiceNow, PagerDuty, Microsoft and AWS through native connectors and MCP. App Builder turns plain language into apps. AI Defense governs the agents and Splunk AI Agent Monitoring traces every step.

chapters.title: Mission assurance for the nation's capital
chapters.body: Dominion owns the main electric system that feeds Joint Base Myer-Henderson Hall and the Pentagon, serves more than 300 federal sites and is exploring on-base generation with the Navy at Yorktown. Splunk Cloud is FedRAMP High and holds a DoD IL5 provisional authorization.

chapters.title: CIP-015: re-architecting access to storage
chapters.body: CIP-015 asks Dominion to monitor inside the ESP, retain anomalous-activity data until each evaluation closes, and protect that data from deletion or tampering. Our teams are reshaping how Splunk Cloud stores and reaches this data: hot detections in Splunk Cloud, full-fidelity data in Dominion-owned S3 read in place by Federated Search, and evidence archived for audits. See our current work together

chapters.title: Two companies, one future, one fabric
chapters.body: The proposed NextEra combination would create the world's largest regulated electric utility business. Federated search lets both SOCs see each other's risk on Day 1 without migrating a byte, while agents manage the integration workload.

threats.name: VOLTZITE / Volt Typhoon at ICS Stage 2
threats.body: Manipulated engineering workstation software to extract configuration files and alarm data, probing which conditions trigger shutdowns.
threats.counter: Engineering workstation behavior baselines (UEBA), Cyber Vision INSM, LOTL hunts in ES.

threats.name: SYLVANITE inside a U.S. electric utility
threats.body: Initial-access broker that exploited Ivanti and extracted Active Directory credentials, then handed footholds to VOLTZITE.
threats.counter: Edge-device exploit detections, AD credential-theft analytics, Triage Agent for fast disposition.

threats.name: KAMACITE mapping U.S. control loops
threats.body: Four months of scanning internet-exposed HMIs, drives, meters and cellular gateways in sequence to map whole control loops.
threats.counter: ARI exposure analytics; Secure Firewall and ISE segmentation; Talos-informed blocking.

threats.name: ELECTRUM attack on Distributed Energy Resources
threats.body: First major coordinated DER attack anywhere, Poland, Dec 2025. Directly relevant to Dominion's solar fleet and mandated VPP pilot.
threats.counter: DER telemetry monitoring at Edge Hub; aggregator API anomaly detection.

threats.name: OT-capable ransomware
threats.body: Ransomware hitting industrial organizations up 64% year over year, 3,300 organizations; average OT dwell time 42 days.
threats.counter: ES Premier + SOAR containment; Splunk Attack Analyzer on initial lures.

threats.name: 24-day exploit window
threats.body: Median 24 days between ICS vulnerability disclosure and public exploit; ~4% exploited at disclosure.
threats.counter: ARI + Cyber Vision vulnerability matching; risk-based prioritization of internet-reachable assets.

threats.name: Physical attacks and drones
threats.body: 3,500+ physical incidents shared with E-ISAC in 2025, 3% disrupting operations; ballistic attacks most concerning; drones an emerging risk.
threats.counter: Converged correlation of PACS, Meraki MV, gunshot and UAS detection with cyber events.

threats.name: GridEx VIII: heat dome over Data Center Alley
threats.body: National exercise scenario combined data center failures, telecom cuts to control rooms, insiders and a leadership deepfake.
threats.counter: ITSI cross-domain service health; UEBA insider analytics; out-of-band verification agents.

threats.name: Agentic AI privilege creep
threats.body: CISA warns agentic AI expands attack surface and privilege creep; start low-risk and avoid broad access to critical systems.
threats.counter: AI Defense policy, human approval gates, Splunk AI Agent Monitoring traces.

threats.name: AI in OT: drift and safety bypass
threats.body: Joint CISA/NSA/FBI guidance flags OT process-model drift and safety-process bypass as key AI-in-OT risks.
threats.counter: Model evaluation and drift detection; advisory-only agents for OT; DefenseClaw fail-closed at the edge.

threats.name: Third-party and vendor compromise
threats.body: Dominion's 10-K notes facility systems are "not completely isolated from external networks" and vendors may be compromised.
threats.counter: SOAR playbook implementing the Vendor Compromise Response Plan; SEA session control.

threats.name: Merger-window social engineering
threats.body: Long, public regulatory windows (through 2H 2027) are a classic lure for BEC, fake integration portals and HR-themed phishing.
threats.counter: Malware Reversing and Phishing agent; brand-impersonation detections; Duo phishing-resistant MFA.

research.title: Monitor and evaluate anomalous activity inside the ESP
research.body: INSM applies to networks inside the Electronic Security Perimeter of high impact BES Cyber Systems and medium impact systems with External Routable Connectivity. Entities must detect and evaluate anomalous network activity. Effective Oct 1, 2028, control centers first.
research.so: Hot, searchable data in Splunk Cloud for ES Premier detections and analyst evaluation; Cyber Vision and IE sensors as the INSM collection point.

research.title: Retain anomalous-activity data until the action is complete
research.body: Entities retain INSM data tied to anomalous activity at least until the R1.3 evaluation is complete. They choose which data types to discard quickly, keep briefly or keep longer. Full packet capture that is not relevant to anomalies does not have to be kept.
research.so: A tiered retention policy per data type: metadata and detections hot, full-fidelity flows and PCAP in low-cost storage, evidence packages archived.

research.title: Protect INSM data from unauthorized deletion or modification
research.body: NERC lists protective and detective controls: access limited to authorized personnel, systems with built-in integrity safeguards, and segmenting the INSM system onto an isolated network separate from the monitored BES Cyber System.
research.so: Role-based access with audited deletes, immutable copies for retained evidence, and an INSM data path that does not share trust with the OT network it watches.

research.title: BCSI may live in the cloud, with key management choices
research.body: Since Jan 1, 2024, NERC standards accommodate BES Cyber System Information in cloud services. With entity-managed keys the provider cannot decrypt BCSI, which simplifies evidence. With mutually managed keys, provider personnel fall into the entity access program.
research.so: Decide early whether INSM data in Splunk Cloud or S3 counts as BCSI, and who holds the keys. This drives where each tier can live.

research.title: Splunk-managed archive for long-term evidence
research.body: Dynamic Data Active Archive keeps expired index data in a Splunk-managed archive for up to 3,650 days. Restores land within about 24 hours and stay searchable for 30 days. Sold in 500 GB increments with 10% extra DDAS for restores.
research.so: Fits R2 evidence that must survive audits without staying in searchable storage.

research.title: Customer-owned S3 storage for aged index data
research.body: Dynamic Data Self Storage moves expired data to a bucket Dominion owns. Federated search over DDSS datasets is now documented through a Splunk-native DDSS data catalog in AWS, including restores from Glacier storage classes.
research.so: Dominion controls the bucket, keys and retention lock settings, which strengthens the R3 and BCSI story.

research.title: Route full-fidelity data to S3 at ingest and search it in place
research.body: On Splunk Cloud 10.4.2604 and later, an Amazon S3 dataset can serve both as an Ingest Processor destination and as a Federated Search source. Constraint: the destination bucket must not have Object Lock turned on.
research.so: Recommendation: pair the write bucket with versioning and replication to a separate Object Lock bucket, so R3 immutability holds without breaking the pipeline.

research.title: Search Parquet, JSON or CSV in S3 without re-ingesting
research.body: Federated Search for Amazon S3 reads CSV, newline JSON, Parquet, ORC, Avro and XML, including data written by Edge Processor and ingest actions. DDSS format needs the DDSS dataset path instead.
research.so: Analysts query cold INSM data from the same ES and SPL workflow, so access to storage is re-architected without a second tool.

tiers.d: Cyber Vision sensors in IE switches and existing INSM taps. Edge Processor on Dominion infrastructure filters, masks BCSI fields and routes by data type.
Detections, metadata and anomaly context stay hot for ES Premier correlation, UEBA and SOAR response. This is the R1 evaluation workspace.
Full-fidelity flows and PCAP slices routed at ingest, plus aged indexes in DDSS. Federated Search reads both in place for R2 investigations.
DDAA for evidence packages up to 10 years. Replicated Object Lock copies and audited deletes demonstrate R3 protection.
A CIP Evidence Agent assembles R1 to R3 evidence per anomaly, from detection to closure, with a human approval gate before anything is filed.

questions: Which INSM data types do you plan to keep hot, keep briefly or discard (R2 retention chart)?
Does INSM data in Splunk Cloud or S3 meet your BCSI definition, and will you hold your own keys?
What is your searchable retention per index, and how much of it is driven by audit rather than detection?
Is any S3 bucket in the design already under Object Lock, and who owns the AWS account?
Which control centers come first before Oct 1, 2028, and when do medium impact sites with ERC follow?
How will EACMS and PACS coverage, which FERC directed NERC to address, change the data volume?

support.d: Map each storage tier to CIP-015 evidence: hot detections for R1 evaluation, retention by data type for R2, and tamper protection for R3.
Decide early whether INSM data in Splunk Cloud or S3 counts as BCSI and who holds the encryption keys, because that decides where each tier can live.
Keep full-fidelity INSM data in Dominion-owned S3 through Ingest Processor datasets or DDSS, searchable in place with Federated Search, so analysts stay in one console.
Resolve the Object Lock constraint up front. Ingest Processor cannot write to an Object Lock bucket, so pair the write bucket with versioning and replication to a locked copy.
Use the Splunk-managed archive (DDAA) for audit evidence packages up to 10 years, so retention grows without growing searchable storage.
